evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep asks 'Do you have about ten minutes to run through that with me?' and 'Before I kinda hop in here, do you have any like, top of concerns or questions that I can help you answer?' — no framing of the 10–15 minute timeline + dependable quote promise, no wait for a yes before moving to probing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Benjamin), moving day (October 11th), origin (3751 north central express way and park in Minney Texas), destination (1110 drive in Melissa, Texas), property type (two bedroom apartment on third floor at origin; 1600 square foot house two stories at destination), size (1600 sq ft destination given). All four asked.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive probing: 'Before I kinda hop in here, do you have any like, top of concerns or questions that I can help you answer?' comes at the very start, but then the rep immediately launches into 'we do have you moving from...' and detailed logistics probing (large items, boxes, access, stairs) before circling back. Technically asked early but buried under immediate probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises frame-and-wall concerns ('frame breakdown'), mattress protection concern, and TV-boxing concern. Rep provides answers but does not probe deeper with 'tell me more about that' or similar — answers are brief and move on. Example: Customer asks 'Should I get mattress covers?' Rep answers 'We do have things to protect the mattresses for the move but really up to you if you wanted to get, like, one of those little plastics leaves' — no follow-up dig.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection. Rep acknowledges concerns individually but never reflects back: 'So what I'm hearing is ___, ___, and ___. Did I get all of it?' Never attempted.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment → house), floors/stories (third floor with stairs at origin; two stories at destination), large items (couch, TV 65–70 inch, TV stand/dresser, totes, dining room table, bar stools, large mirror, two desks), box count (35–40), garage/detached (none at origin), parking/access at origin (15–20 yards from building to parking lot), access at destination (driveway + 10–15 feet parking), interior stairs (customer uncertain, wife not on phone — rep notes for crew but doesn't press). Nearly all seven probed.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked. Rep discusses boxes and materials for TV protection but never offers packing service ('Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?').
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes. 'Approximately how many boxes would you say you all will have? Our average is about 25 to 354 unit at this size.' Customer responds based on prior move estimate.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full. 'Right now we have you slided for four to five hours from start to finish with this move and based off the information that you gave to me, I mean I wouldn't make any adjustments to it.' Provides typical range for size + personalized to customer's specifics (two desks, large items, short distance).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full. '...two and a half hour minimum which will be over that anyway. But if it only takes three to four hours, that's all you all end up paying for anyway.' Covers 2.5-hour minimum and pay-for-time-used framing. Trip fee not explicitly mentioned, but no-guess confidence is embedded in the estimate delivery.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent, and moves directly into Two Promises section without a pause for customer reaction to the estimate.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full. 'if we don't arrive in a window that we say we will, the money is automatically deducted out your final vehicle payment' — covers discount terms clearly.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full. 'we damage coverage that does cover-up to $2,000 for any incidentals that's already included in your service' — $2,000, no-deductible framing implied (no mention of deductible or fine print), included in rate (not an add-on).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. No 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar. Rep moves from Two Promises directly into crew introduction and general final questions without looping back to confirm the promises landed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Full (genuine, not throwaway). 'And then, yeah, do you have any other questions that I can answer?' — asked as genuine, though could be stronger as 'What's still concerning you about this move?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False. Never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never. Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or recognizable version. Call ends with 'Well Benjamin, thank you so much for answering my call' and logistics/contact info, but no explicit booking ask.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: False. No mention of rate lock or no-deposit guarantee.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Full. Date (October 11th), arrival window (8:30 AM), crew introduction (Noa), addresses (3751 north central expressway/unit 5313 to 1110 drive in Melissa), move duration (4–5 hours). Phone/text/email follow-up confirmed. No specific crew size mentioned, but otherwise complete.

top_strength: Chauntelle gathered comprehensive logistics details (origin/destination, property types, large items, box count, access constraints, stair configuration) and delivered the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) fully and clearly without ambiguity.
coaching_note: Add the quid-pro-quo time-box and dependable-quote promise at the very start with a real wait-for-yes before probing; probe deeper ('tell me more about that') on customer concerns instead of one-question-and-answer; ask 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate and hold the silence; and most critically, ask an explicit closing question ('Would you like our help with your move?') before ending the call — you never asked for the business.
